items.title: Section: Proper-Practice Veneration Closes — Guarding the Precepts and Training in Every Perfection, Named as the Highest Offering of All

items.zh: 如是守護菩薩所受尸羅律儀，於奢摩他、毘鉢舍那、菩提分法精勤修學，亦於一切波羅蜜多及諸攝事正勤修學。是名菩薩於如來所正行供養。如是供養為最第一、最上、最勝、最妙、無上。如是供養，過前所說具一切種財敬供養，百倍、千倍，乃至鄔波尼殺曇倍。由此十相，應知是名具一切種供養如來。如供養佛，如是供養若法、若僧。隨其所應，當知亦爾。
items.en: Likewise, guarding the bodhisattva precepts and vows one has received, diligently training in calming and insight practice and in the factors of awakening, and also correctly and diligently training in every perfection and every means of gathering beings — this too is called a bodhisattva's proper-practice veneration in the Tathāgata's presence. Veneration of this kind is first, highest, most excellent, most sublime, and unsurpassed. Veneration of this kind exceeds every kind of wealth-and-respect veneration already fully described, by a hundred times, a thousand times, even by an incalculable multiple beyond counting. Through these ten marks, one should understand this to be called complete veneration of the Tathāgata in every one of its kinds. Just as one venerates the Buddha, so too one venerates the Dharma and the Saṅgha, each according to what is fitting — one should understand this in just the same way.

items.title: Section: Six Kinds of Heightened Aspiration Open — the Buddha as an Unsurpassed Field of Merit, and an Unsurpassed Great Benefactor

items.zh: 如是菩薩於三寶所，由十種相興供養時，應緣如來發起六種增上意樂。一者、無上大功德田，增上意樂；二者、無上有大恩德，增上意樂；
items.en: When bodhisattvas of this kind, in the presence of the three jewels, raise veneration through the ten marks already described, they should, taking the Tathāgata as their object, give rise to six kinds of heightened aspiration. First, the heightened aspiration of reflecting on the Tathāgata as an unsurpassed field of great merit; second, the heightened aspiration of reflecting on the Tathāgata as one who has shown unsurpassed, great kindness to beings.

items.title: Section: Supreme Among Every Footed and Footless Being — the Buddha as Ghee, Finest of All That Comes From Milk

items.zh: 三者、一切無足、二足及多足等有情中尊，增上意樂；
items.en: Third, the heightened aspiration of reflecting that the Tathāgata is supreme among beings without feet, with two feet, and with many feet, and every being of this kind. The Compendium of Synonyms explains: footless beings are such as snakes; two-footed beings are such as humans; four-footed beings are such as cattle; many-footed beings are such as centipedes. The Tathāgata is, among all these beings, first in three respects: by way of restless stirring, by way of what one's body depends upon, and by way of mind. This is called being supreme among every kind of being.

items.title: Section: Rare as the Udumbara Flower, Alone in This World-System, the Complete Basis of Every Benefit — the Sixth Aspiration Closes the Set

items.zh: 四者、猶如鄔曇妙華極難值遇，增上意樂；五者、獨一出現三千大千世界，增上意樂；六者、一切世出世間功德圓滿一切義依，增上意樂。由是六種增上意樂，於如來所，若於如來法所、僧所，少分思惟而興供養，尚獲無量大功德果，何況其多。
items.en: Fourth, the heightened aspiration of reflecting that the Tathāgata is as extraordinarily difficult to encounter as the exquisite udumbara flower; fifth, the heightened aspiration of reflecting that the Tathāgata appears alone within this great trichiliocosm of three thousand worlds; sixth, the heightened aspiration of reflecting that the Tathāgata's every worldly and transcendent virtue has reached complete perfection, becoming the very basis of every genuine benefit. Through these six kinds of heightened aspiration, even a small measure of reflection while raising veneration in the presence of the Tathāgata, or of the Tathāgata's Dharma, or of the Saṅgha, already obtains an immeasurable fruit of great merit and virtue — how much more so, then, if that reflection is sustained abundantly.

items.title: Section: Approaching Good Friends Opens — Seven Questions Frame an Entire Section

items.zh: 復次，菩薩成就幾相，能為善友？由幾種相，善友不虛？成就幾相，令善友性作信依處？復有幾種善友菩薩，於所化生為善友事？菩薩幾種親近善友？由幾種想，於善友所聽聞正法？由幾種處，於善友所聽聞法時，於說法師不作異意？
items.en: Furthermore: by how many marks does a bodhisattva succeed in being a genuine spiritual friend? By how many marks is such friendship never empty or false? By how many marks does the very nature of being a spiritual friend become a genuinely trustworthy support? By how many further ways does a bodhisattva who is a spiritual friend actually act on behalf of the beings they are guiding? By how many ways does a bodhisattva properly approach a spiritual friend? By how many kinds of reflection does one listen to the true teaching in a spiritual friend's presence? And on how many points, when listening to the teaching in a spiritual friend's presence, should one never form a contrary opinion of the teacher delivering it?

items.title: Section: The Eight Marks of a Complete Spiritual Friend Open — Unbroken Discipline, Genuine Learning, and Real Realisation

items.zh: 當知菩薩成就八支，能為善友眾相圓滿。一者、住戒。於諸菩薩律儀戒中妙善安住，無缺無穿。二者、多聞。覺慧成就。三者、具證。得修所成隨一勝善，逮奢摩他、毘鉢舍那。
items.en: One should understand that bodhisattvas who accomplish eight elements are able to be spiritual friends whose every mark is completely fulfilled. First, dwelling in discipline: excellently and correctly abiding within the bodhisattva precepts and vows, without lapse and without breach. Second, genuine learning: the accomplishment of a discerning intelligence. Third, genuine realisation: having attained, through cultivated wisdom, any one of the excellent, wholesome states, reaching calming practice and insight practice.

items.title: Section: Compassion, Fearlessness, and Patience — the Sixteen Classical Reflections That Let a Teacher Absorb Any Insult

items.zh: 四者、哀愍。內具慈悲，能捨自己現法樂住，精勤無怠饒益於他。五者、無畏。為他宣說正法教時非由恐怖忘失念辯。六者、堪忍。於他輕笑、調弄、鄙言、違拒等事，非愛言路、種種惡行皆悉能忍。
items.en: Fourth, compassion: possessing genuine loving-kindness and compassion within, able to set aside one's own present ease dwelling in meditative absorption, diligently and tirelessly benefiting others. Fifth, fearlessness: when proclaiming the true teaching for others' sake, never losing mindfulness or eloquence through fear. Sixth, patience: able to bear entirely with others' mockery, ridicule, coarse and contemptible speech, and open defiance, and with every kind of unwelcome word or ill conduct.

items.title: Section: Tirelessness Before Four Assemblies, and Skilful Speech's Eight Qualities — Even Reaching "Ninety Days on a Single Word"

items.zh: 七者、無倦。其力充強，能多思擇，處在四眾說正法時，言無謇澁，心不疲厭。八者、善詞。語具圓滿，不壞法性，言詞辯了。
items.en: Seventh, tirelessness: possessing genuinely strong physical and mental capacity, able to reflect and discern extensively over a long time, so that when teaching the true dharma before the four assemblies, one's speech never stumbles and one's mind never grows fatigued or weary. Eighth, skilful speech: language that is fully complete in every one of its qualities, never damaging the true nature of reality, and eloquent, clear, and fully understood.

items.title: Section: Guidance That Is Never Empty — the Five Marks Behind Genuinely Effective Teaching

items.zh: 若諸菩薩具五種相，眾德相應，能為善友所作不虛。一者、於他先欲求作利益安樂；二者、於彼利益安樂如實了知，無顛倒覺；三者、於彼善權方便順儀說法，隨眾堪受調伏事中，有能有力；四者、饒益心無厭倦；五者、具足平等大悲，於諸有情劣中勝品心無偏黨。
items.en: Bodhisattvas who possess five marks, joined together with many virtues, are able to be spiritual friends whose guidance is never empty or in vain. First, wishing beforehand to bring benefit and ease to others. Second, correctly and without distorted understanding knowing what genuinely constitutes that benefit and ease. Third, possessing both the capacity and the strength to teach the dharma through skilful and fitting means, suited to whatever degree of discipline the audience can actually receive. Fourth, a mind that benefits others without ever growing weary. Fifth, possessing a genuinely equal great compassion, with no partiality of mind among the lesser, the middling, and the excellent among the various kinds of beings.

items.title: Section: A Trustworthy Basis of Faith Opens — Dignified Deportment So Complete Even Its Absence Is Never Seen

items.zh: 若諸菩薩成就五相，令善友性作信依處，令他遠聞極生淨信，何況親覩。一者、勝妙。威儀圓滿、威儀寂靜、威儀具足，一切支分皆無躁動。二者、敦肅。三業現行無掉無擾。
items.en: Bodhisattvas who accomplish five marks make the very nature of being a spiritual friend into a genuine basis of faith, such that others, merely hearing of them from far away, already give rise to the purest faith — how much more so, then, upon actually beholding them in person. First, dignified deportment: complete, tranquil, and fully accomplished deportment, with not a single limb or part of the body showing any restless movement. Second, grave sincerity: body, speech, and mind alike showing, in their actual activity, neither agitation nor disturbance.

items.title: Section: No Pretence, No Envy, No Excess — Closing the Marks of a Trustworthy Basis of Faith

items.zh: 三者、無矯。不為誑他，故思詐現嚴整威儀。四者、無嫉。終不於他說法所得利養恭敬生不堪忍，而常自勵請他說法；復恒勸餘於彼廣施利養恭敬，無諂偽心。又常於他其心純淨，見彼說法及得財敬，深生隨喜。如自所獲利養恭敬，心生歡喜，見他所得利養恭敬，其心歡喜復過於是。五者、儉約。尠儲器物，隨得隨捨。
items.en: Third, freedom from pretence: never deliberately staging a falsely dignified, orderly bearing simply in order to deceive others into trusting oneself. Fourth, freedom from envy: never once unable to bear another's gain in offerings and respect from teaching the dharma, but instead constantly urging oneself on to invite them to teach, and constantly encouraging others to give that teacher generous offerings and respect, entirely free of any flattering or false intent. Moreover, one's mind remains genuinely pure towards others at all times, so that upon seeing another teach and receive offerings and respect, one feels deep, genuine rejoicing — exactly as one feels joy upon receiving offerings and respect oneself, and, upon seeing another receive them, feeling a joy that surpasses even that. Fifth, frugality: keeping very few stored possessions, giving away at once whatever one happens to receive.

items.title: Section: Five Duties of a Spiritual Friend — Correcting, Reminding, Instructing, Admonishing, and Teaching

items.zh: 善友菩薩由五種相，於所化生為善友事。一、能諫舉，二、能令憶，三、能教授，四、能教誡，五、能說法。如是諸句廣辯應知如聲聞地。教授教誡，廣說如前力種性品。
items.en: Bodhisattvas who are spiritual friends, through five marks, perform the actual work of a spiritual friend for the beings they are guiding. First, correcting through admonishment; second, restoring memory; third, instructing; fourth, admonishing according to discipline; fifth, teaching the dharma. One should understand every one of these in full detail as already explained in the Śrāvaka Stage. Instruction and admonishment according to discipline are explained in full detail, as before, in the chapter on the power of spiritual lineage.

blocks.text: Why practice is the highest offering, and the qualities of a true spiritual friend (compare Day 209).

"Guarding the precepts and vows received, training in calm and insight and the factors of awakening, and in every perfection": "this veneration surpasses all material veneration a hundredfold, a thousandfold". Master Cháng Bǎi: the first nine are material offerings, the tenth the offering of Dharma.

The Buddha as an unsurpassed field of merit (Master Cháng Bǎi: seed sown in salty soil yields nothing); as an unsurpassed benefactor; "supreme among beings with no feet, two feet, or many feet"; "as hard to encounter as the udumbara flower"; appearing alone in a world-system; and the basis of every benefit.

Eight marks: discipline, learning, realisation, compassion, fearlessness, patience ("able to endure mockery, ridicule, crude words": Master Cháng Bǎi: like a flower falling on an elephant), tirelessness, and skilful speech. Venerable Miào Jìng distinguishes acquired wisdom from innate.
Five marks make guidance effective, starting with "wishing beforehand to benefit others" and "knowing correctly what benefits".
"Deportment complete, tranquil, with no restless movement." Master Cháng Bǎi: Master Hongyi always tapped a chair before sitting, so as not to crush an insect on it. Free of pretence and envy.

quiz.q: How much does the treatise say proper-practice veneration surpasses wealth-and-respect veneration?
options: a hundred, a thousand times, up to an upaniṣad-fold
quiz.why: "This veneration surpasses all the wealth-and-respect veneration described earlier a hundredfold, a thousandfold, up to an upaniṣad-fold." Venerable Miào Jìng: practising calm and insight, you needn't move — sitting right here is proper-practice veneration.

quiz.q: Among the ten kinds of veneration, how does Master Cháng Bǎi divide material from dharma offering?
options: the first nine are material, the tenth (proper practice) is dharma offering
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the first nine are material offerings, the tenth is the offering of dharma.

quiz.q: The first heightened aspiration — "unsurpassed field of merit." What image does Master Cháng Bǎi use for differences among fields?
options: farming: salty soil yields nothing and spoils the seed; offering to arhats is like rich but narrow land
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: seed sown in salty soil produces no rice and is ruined; offering to arhats and pratyekabuddhas is like rich soil, much harvest yet limited land. Venerable Miào Jìng: the Buddha is a good field, enabling supreme merit.

quiz.q: What are the fourth and fifth heightened aspirations?
options: as rare as the udumbara flower; appearing alone in the great trichiliocosm
quiz.why: "Fourth, that the Tathāgata is as hard to encounter as the udumbara flower; fifth, that he appears alone in the great trichiliocosm." Master Cháng Bǎi: the udumbara blooms once in three thousand years.

quiz.q: What are the first three of the eight marks of a spiritual friend?
quiz.why: "First, dwelling in discipline … without lapse or breach. Second, learning — accomplished in understanding and wisdom. Third, realisation — attaining calm and insight." Master Cháng Bǎi: learning lets one know the dharma, avoid evil, abandon the meaningless, attain nirvāṇa.

quiz.q: On patience, what images does Master Cháng Bǎi use for different ways of receiving insult?
options: a flower falling on an elephant is barely felt; a bird hit by a stone suffers sharply
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: like a flower falling on an elephant — hardly felt, quickly falling off; versus a little bird struck by a stone — painful and distressing.

quiz.q: On deportment, what habit of Master Hongyi does Master Cháng Bǎi mention?
options: always tapping a chair before sitting so as not to crush any insect
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: before sitting, Master Hongyi always tapped the chair so as not to crush any insect on it. Venerable Miào Jìng: "dūn" is sincere, "sù" respectful and solemn.
